subject: Mathematics
title: Limits, Continuity and Differentiability
summary: A limit describes the value f(x) approaches as x approaches a; it exists when the left-hand and right-hand limits are equal and finite.
Indeterminate forms (0/0, ∞/∞, 1^∞, 0 × ∞, ∞ − ∞) are handled by factorisation, rationalisation, standard limits, series expansion or L'Hôpital's rule.
f is continuous at a if lim f(x) = f(a). f is differentiable at a if the left and right derivatives are equal; differentiability implies continuity, but not conversely (|x| at 0).

formulas.name: Trigonometric limits
formulas.formula: lim sin x/x = 1;  lim tan x/x = 1;  lim (1 − cos x)/x² = 1/2  (x → 0, radians)

formulas.name: Exponential and log limits
formulas.formula: lim (eˣ − 1)/x = 1;  lim (aˣ − 1)/x = ln a;  lim ln(1 + x)/x = 1  (x → 0)

formulas.name: 1^∞ form
formulas.formula: lim f^g = e^{lim g(f − 1)} when f → 1, g → ∞;  lim (1 + 1/x)ˣ = e;  lim (1 + x)^{1/x} = e

formulas.name: L'Hôpital's rule
formulas.formula: for 0/0 or ∞/∞: lim f/g = lim f′/g′
formulas.mistake: Differentiate numerator and denominator separately — not the quotient.

formulas.name: Series expansions
formulas.formula: eˣ = 1 + x + x²/2! + …;  sin x = x − x³/3! + …;  cos x = 1 − x²/2! + …;  ln(1 + x) = x − x²/2 + …;  tan x = x + x³/3 + …

formulas.name: Rational functions at infinity
formulas.formula: degree num < den → 0;  equal → ratio of leading coefficients;  num > den → ±∞

formulas.name: Continuity
formulas.formula: f continuous at a ⇔ lim (x→a) f(x) = f(a)

formulas.name: Differentiability
formulas.formula: Lf′(a) = lim (h→0⁻) (f(a + h) − f(a))/h;  Rf′(a) similarly;  differentiable ⇔ Lf′(a) = Rf′(a)
formulas.note: Differentiable ⇒ continuous, but continuous ⇏ differentiable (|x| at 0).

formulas.name: Sandwich theorem
formulas.formula: g(x) ≤ f(x) ≤ h(x) and lim g = lim h = L ⇒ lim f = L

examples.title: Continuity condition
examples.problem: f(x) = (x³ − 1)/(x − 1) for x ≠ 1 and f(1) = k. Find k for continuity.

topics.title: Rationalisation
topics.explain: For limits with square roots like (√(x + 1) − 1)/x, multiply by the conjugate to remove the 0/0 form.

topics.title: Limits at infinity with roots
topics.explain: For √(x² + x) − x as x → ∞, rationalise to get x/(√(x² + x) + x) → 1/2.

topics.title: Continuity of standard functions
topics.explain: Polynomials, sin, cos, eˣ are continuous everywhere; rational functions except where the denominator is 0; log x for x > 0; [x] is discontinuous at integers.

topics.title: Algebra of continuous functions
topics.explain: Sum, difference, product and composition of continuous functions are continuous; quotient too, where the denominator isn't zero.

topics.title: Intermediate value theorem
topics.explain: If f is continuous on [a, b] and k lies between f(a) and f(b), then f(c) = k for some c in (a, b) — used to show an equation has a root.

topics.title: Non-differentiable points
topics.explain: Corners (|x − a|), cusps, vertical tangents (x^{1/3} at 0) and discontinuities. |f(x)| may fail to be differentiable where f(x) = 0 and changes sign.
